region: SE Brazil coast (RJ–SP–ES–PR–SC · Guanabara → Ilhabela + Costa Verde / Lagos)

good.title: World Cleanup Day: Argonauta, Tamar and Aquário clean Praia do Itaguá in Ubatuba
good.summary: On 19 Sep (from 8h30 at Praça da Baleia), Aquário de Ubatuba, Instituto Argonauta and Fundação Projeto Tamar lead a shore cleanup on Praia do Itaguá with PESM Picinguaba, APA Marinha LN, Mar Sem Lixo and partners — sorting and logging litter as citizen science. Marks ~30 years of the local anti-marine-litter campaign started in the 1990s.

good.title: Cleanup Day 2026: Instituto Supereco mobilizes volunteers on Santos beach
good.summary: Tecendo as Águas (Supereco / Petrobras Socioambiental) joins the 19 Sep global Cleanup Day from 9h on the beach in front of Etec Dona Escolástica Rosa (Av. Bartolomeu de Gusmão). 2025 Santos actions removed 53+ kg on Gonzaga and 1.46 t from Jardim São Manoel mangrove — data-driven litter removal for the Santos estuary corridor.

good.title: World Cleanup Day mutirão set for Flamengo beach and Marina da Glória
good.summary: Projeto Tatuí (Instituto Ecológico Aqualung) and Axia Marina da Glória schedule a 19 Sep collection gincana (9h–12h30) targeting small plastic fragments before they reach Guanabara. Top collectors get sustainability course scholarships; the marina already removes about 3–4 t of floating trash yearly. Shirt art honors two recent boto-cinza calves.
good.location: Praia do Flamengo / Marina da Glória, Rio

good.title: Rio Ocean Week: sanitation framed as the path to cleaner Guanabara beaches
good.summary: At Museu do Amanhã (17 Sep), Águas do Rio highlighted R$6.4 bn invested since concession start, dry-weather collectors ringing Guanabara Bay, and ~134 million liters/day of raw sewage kept out of the bay — arguing urban river cleanup returns Flamengo/Glória-type beaches to the city and supports the blue economy.

good.title: World Cleanup Day: Biomar mutirões include São Sebastião beach cleanup
good.summary: Rede Biomar (Coral Vivo, Baleia Jubarte and partners) is running September cleanups with citizen science — sorting, weighing, and logging trash. São Sebastião’s Praia da Barra do Sahy action was set for 15 Sep; the network has removed about 17 t since 2018. Plastic dominated past editions. Useful context for shore entries and shoreline dive staging.

good.title: São Sebastião Cleanup Day warm-up removes 8.78 kg near Convento de São Francisco
good.summary: On 16 Sep, Instituto Supereco with SEMAM and Programa Mar Sem Lixo logged 600 cigarette butts, plastics, styrofoam and glass near the historic convent — anticipating the 19 Sep global day. Projeto Baleia Jubarte staff joined; kids from Projeto Cidadão Criança took part. Small haul, strong local education signal on the LN SP dive corridor.

good.title: Clean Up The World 2026 mobilizes Rio beaches plus Ilha Grande points
good.summary: The 24th Brazilian edition runs 19 Sep (10h–13h) with biodegradable collection bags and recycling partners. Meetups include Copacabana, Ipanema, Barra, Macumba, Grumari, Niterói (Itaipu/Itacoatiara/Camboinhas), Búzios (Praia Rasa), and Ilha Grande Praia Preta and Dois Rios with CEADS-UERJ — direct shoreline litter removal across dive and swim corridors.

good.title: Baixada works aim to keep 71 million liters/day of sewage out of Guanabara rivers
good.summary: Águas do Rio starts R$466 million sanitation works in Duque de Caxias and Nilópolis to intercept about 71 million liters of sewage daily from the Farias, Pavuna, and Sarapuí rivers — part of the Guanabara Bay recovery basin that feeds Rio’s eastern maritime approaches. Benefits ~325 thousand residents; microtunneling (“tatuzinhos”) limits street disruption.

good.title: Potential shark nursery mapped in the Ilha Grande–Sepetiba complex
good.summary: A PROSHARK study with UFRJ and UNIRIO documented six pregnant females — spinner, blacktip, and sand tiger (mangona) — from records spanning 2006–2024, the first time all three species were recorded pregnant in the area. Two of the species are threatened in Brazil; the authors argue the estuary may be a reproductive refuge and a conservation priority. The paper appears in the Brazilian Journal of Biology; ((o))eco covered it on 8 Sep.

good.title: Paraty’s new sewage treatment plant advances — bioreactor base poured
good.summary: Concrete for the bioreactor base (~140 m³) marks a structural milestone on Paraty’s new ETE, a Prefeitura–Estado–INEA project with FECAM funds. Phase one targets ~4 million liters/day (~45% of local population) with modular expansion planned; operation is expected around April 2028. Framed as protection for UNESCO-listed Paraty and Ilha Grande Bay water quality — long-term balneabilidade and dive-shore context.

good.title: Ilha Grande shark project schedules beach + underwater Clean Up Day in Angra
good.summary: Projeto Tubarões da Baía da Ilha Grande (IBRACON / Petrobras Socioambiental) set 19 Sep at Praia do Anil: shore cleanup 9–10h and scuba debris collection 10–14h near monitoring sites (Aquamaster logistics), plus species exhibits. Materials will be sorted and classified; registered volunteers get certificates. Ties research visibility to practical marine litter removal.
good.location: Praia do Anil, Angra dos Reis

good.title: Sabesp intercepts nearly 2,000 t of trash and grease from Baixada Santista sewers
good.summary: Jan–Jun 2026 removals total 1,966.3 t before pumping/treatment (Santos 574 t, São Vicente 433 t), including plastics, diapers, and grease that otherwise risk overflows toward the estuary and beaches. Monthly average fell ~18% vs 2025. Preventive work covers 353 lift stations and 18 treatment plants — practical sewage-to-sea risk reduction for the Santos/São Vicente corridor.

good.title: Ilhabela humpback season highlights recovery and responsible tourism
good.summary: Projeto Baleia Jubarte estimates more than 30,000 humpbacks in the Brazilian population after the hunting ban and Lei 7.643/1987. Ilhabela logged a municipal record of 836 sightings in 2025, with the first 2026 Brazilian sighting again there in April. Peak is typically June–July; the town holds a “Cidade Amiga das Baleias” seal and stresses IBAMA approach rules.

good.title: Baía da Ilha Grande consolidates as a shark research and refuge hotspot
good.summary: PROSHARK monitoring with satellite and acoustic tags, drones, and caiçara knowledge is documenting large blacktip aggregations, tiger sharks including a >4.5 m individual nicknamed Big Mama, and tagged females such as Caiçara and Badjeca. The institute is also working on coexistence protocols and sustainable tourism messaging around Angra dos Reis.
good.location: Baía da Ilha Grande, Angra dos Reis

good.title: CMAS Pan-American Spearfishing Championship set for Cabo Frio
good.summary: The men’s and women’s championship runs 3–6 Dec 2026 in Cabo Frio and validates Americas ranking and 2027 World Championship slots. The bulletin cites average visibility around 10–15 m, water about 18–23 °C, and fishing depths to ~30 m on good days across zones including Capões, Dois Irmãos, and Arpoador–Tucuns.

good.title: Mangue Alegria hits 20,000 native seedlings on Guanabara’s Caju shore
good.summary: Águas do Rio with biologist Mário Moscatelli report ~1 ha restored at ETE Alegria (Zona Portuária), 20k mangrove/native seedlings planted and 450 t of trash removed from the forest fringe. Concessionaire says sanitation works already keep ~134 million L/day of raw sewage out of the bay; dry-weather collector belt continues.
good.location: Caju / ETE Alegria, Baía de Guanabara

good.title: Guapimirim mangrove replanting draws back 70+ species on Guanabara shore
good.summary: Projeto Meros do Brasil and Cooperativa Manguezal Fluminense planted 1,250 native red/black/white mangrove seedlings from 2023 in APA Guapimirim; trees now exceed 3 m on ~400 m² once cleared of invasives. Crabs, fish, and birds returned — nursery habitat that buffers erosion and storm energy at the bay’s northern fringe.

good.title: Rare sand-tiger (mangona) surface jump filmed in Ilhabela
good.summary: A tourist filmed Carcharias taurus briefly leaving the surface during a whale-watch trip. A Unifesp zoologist noted the behavior is unusual but consistent with air-gulping for buoyancy; the species is common locally, with no accident reports cited, and presence framed as a healthy-sea signal.

good.title: Ubatuba creates “Ubatuba Azul – Avistamento Consciente”
good.summary: Municipal Decree 9.112 (25 Jun 2026) regulates whale and dolphin watching with training, an operator registry, a seal, and alignment with Portaria IBAMA 117/1996 — including at least 100 m vessel distance and no swim or dive within 50 m. Partners include Instituto Argonauta, APA Marinha LN, and Instituto Baleia Jubarte.

good.title: Dolphin group filmed alongside fishing boat off Ubatuba
good.summary: Fisher Gustavo Santos recorded dolphins swimming close to his vessel; Mercado do Peixe and local radio shared the clip widely. Coastal feeding associations with boats are known on the Litoral Norte — a wildlife-presence signal for boaters and snorkelers, with the usual reminder not to chase or feed cetaceans.

good.title: Instituto Argonauta frees juvenile humpback “Lena” from fishing gear off Ubatuba
good.summary: Specialized disentanglement teams removed nets and lines from a known juvenile near Ponta Grossa; after release she swam away cleanly on her migration path. Case underscores ghost-gear and entanglement risk on the LN SP whale corridor — call trained responders, do not attempt DIY rescues.

good.title: Projeto Mar de Baleias restarts cetacean watch from Arraial mirantes
good.summary: Funtec Ambiental volunteers monitor small and large cetaceans Tue/Thu/Sat from Mirante do Pontal do Atalaia, logging species, distance, behavior, and human interactions for conservation policy. Shore-based spotting from Atalaia, Boa Vista, and Flávia Alessandra mirantes is encouraged over vessel approaches during whale season.

good.title: Two gray-dolphin (boto-cinza) calves renew hope in Guanabara Bay
good.summary: Maqua/UERJ and Instituto Mar Urbano highlight calves (~2 and ~6 months) in a resident Sotalia guianensis population stuck near ~30 animals for a decade. Biologists stress each pup is precious amid ship noise, bycatch, and pollution; Paquetá–Guapimirim remains a quieter core area. Strong “bay still lives” signal for urban diving and wildlife watching.

good.title: Blacktip females return to Ilha Grande Bay for gestation season
good.summary: Projeto Tubarões da Baía da Ilha Grande (IBRACON) reported winter return of pregnant-season blacktip females, concentrated at Enseada de Piraquara de Fora in Angra. Prior drone work logged 113 individuals there — cited as the largest C. limbatus aggregation in the South Atlantic. Team stresses no recorded human incidents; females expected through about October.
good.location: Piraquara de Fora, Angra dos Reis

good.title: Artisanal fishers remove nearly 24 tonnes of trash in Ubatuba and São Sebastião
good.summary: Programa Mar Sem Lixo paid fishers during the shrimp closed season (Feb–Apr 2026): about 14.8 t in Ubatuba and 9.1 t in São Sebastião, roughly 97% plastic in mangroves. The program has removed more than 164 t on the São Paulo coast since 2023.

good.title: First adult loggerhead (“Anitta”) tagged in Guanabara Bay with Projeto Aruanã
good.summary: A ~108 kg adult female Caretta caretta and juvenile “Shakira” were marked near Magé’s Píer de Piedade after fisher alerts — part of a rising bay presence of an ocean-going threatened species. Tissue samples go to genetics; satellite tags planned. Reinforces Guanabara as feeding habitat and the urgency of bay cleanup for turtles.

good.title: Costão Rochoso underwater census tracks turtles, fish, and corals in Arraial
good.summary: UFF-linked Projeto Costão Rochoso (Petrobras Socioambiental) dives the RESEX with telemetry and photo-ID — 500+ turtles catalogued since 2018, coral color and reef-fish counts, DNA samples to trace Atlantic origins. Scientists warn <3 m tourist approaches stress resting turtles; upwelling keeps cold nutrient-rich water that fuels Arraial’s dive fame.

bad.title: CETESB: 50 Litoral Norte beaches unfit for bathing after rains
bad.summary: The 17 Sep bulletin lists 50 improper points across Caraguatatuba, Ilhabela, São Sebastião, and Ubatuba (116 statewide), including many Ilhabela and Ubatuba sites. Enterococci stayed elevated over five consecutive weeks; the next update is expected around 24 Sep. Treat mainland beach entries and shore diving with caution until runoff clears; offshore island sites are often less tied to fecal indicators — confirm day-of with operators.

bad.title: After heavy rains, 116 São Paulo coast beaches unfit for bathing
bad.summary: Statewide CETESB bulletin (17 Sep): 50 LN + 66 Litoral Sul/Baixada Santista points fail enterococci criteria across 175 monitored sites. G1 lists broad Baixada and South Coast restrictions after multi-day rain — avoid shore entries and nearshore diving for 24h+ after storms; check the weekly map before swim or shore scuba.

bad.title: INEA Niterói: only 24% of monitored points fit for bathing after rains
bad.summary: Bulletin of 17 Sep shows 7 of 29 points própria (24%). Ocean and bay beaches including Camboinhas, Itacoatiara, Itaipu, Icaraí, Charitas and São Francisco are imprópria; Piratininga, Eva, Gragoatá and Sossego remain própria. Heavy recent rain typically drives fecal indicator spikes — check before shore dives or family swims.

bad.title: INEA Rio city: only 39% of points própria — Ipanema and Flamengo still unfit
bad.summary: Analysis of 17 Sep: 24 of 61 points própria. Copacabana (4/4), Grumari, Recreio, Leme and Joatinga stay própria, but Ipanema (0/3), Flamengo, Botafogo, São Conrado and many bay/island points are imprópria; Barra da Tijuca and Leblon are parcial. Weekend swim/dive staging needs point-level checks.

bad.title: Fatal fishing-boat capsize in Saquarema surf
bad.summary: Carlos Magno Espíndola Borges, 56, died after a boat overturned in Itaúna surf after drifting overnight from Canal de Barra Franca; his companion survived. The body was recovered about 10 hours later at Vilatur on 16 Sep. Not a dive incident, but a reminder of boat and sea-user risk on the eastern RJ flank of this brief corridor.

bad.title: INEA and Navy investigate oil sheens in Botafogo cove
bad.summary: TV Globo aerials showed oil-like patches at multiple points in Enseada de Botafogo on 8 Sep, one near the sand. INEA and Capitania teams later reported only a small sheen already dissipating in rough conditions; full identification was limited by weather. The cove is a busy small-boat tourism corridor into Guanabara — watch for residual tar or film if boating or shore diving nearby.

bad.title: Santos hits 100% unfit beaches in CETESB weekly bulletin
bad.summary: All seven monitored Santos points (José Menino through Ponta da Praia) were improper as of 30 Aug, seven of 17 Baixada Santista red flags that week. Enterococci criteria over five weeks; gastroenteritis and other infection risks cited. Estuary/sewage pressure remains a chronic constraint on shore entries along the Santos–São Vicente front.

bad.title: 10.7 m dead humpback found on Itanhaém Centro beach
bad.summary: Instituto Biopesca removed a Megaptera novaeangliae carcass on 28 Aug; advanced decomposition blocked a firm cause, though fishing interaction was suspected. Biologist Eric Comin warned of pathogens, toxic gases, water contamination, and shark attraction — stay clear and call responders. Migration-season reminder for the SP South Coast.

bad.title: Three Magellanic penguins and a dolphin found dead on Baixada Santista beaches
bad.summary: Instituto Biopesca (PMP-BS) recovered three Spheniscus magellanicus on Praia do Maracanã (Praia Grande) and a dolphin in Mongaguá on 24 Aug. Advanced decomposition blocked cause-of-death ID; winter migration and weather may play a role. Public advised to keep distance and call responders — not push animals back to sea.

bad.title: MPF charges shipyards over hazardous waste dumped toward Guanabara Bay
bad.summary: Federal prosecutors charged Selano Trade and PSA Reparos Navais for operating an unlicensed shipyard in Caju for about seven years and abandoning oily waste, gas cylinders, and other hazardous materials that reached bay waters. INEA/DPMA inspection in Feb 2025 documented the site; MPF seeks at least R$1.45 million in environmental reparations.

bad.title: Dead humpback washes up on Praia Grande; public-health warnings issued
bad.summary: Early August stranding at Vila Caiçara/Real drew crowds before Biopesca necropsy sampling and municipal removal. Coverage stressed pathogen and gas risks plus shark attraction from carcass fluids — same migration-season hazard pattern as later Itanhaém. Do not touch stranded cetaceans.

bad.title: INEA: Itaipu sewage outfall keeps chronic pressure on Niterói lagoons
bad.summary: Gerquali technical opinion to the MP says keeping ETE Itaipu discharge ~200 m before Lagoa de Itaipu via Córrego dos Colibris is unfavorable medium/long term. Best path pairs relocating the outfall with stronger nutrient/pathogen treatment; site sits inside PESET class-special waters. Águas de Niterói says effluent meets current standards — lagoon water quality remains a watch item east of Guanabara.

bad.title: Pygmy sperm whale dies after triple stranding and rehab in Cabo Frio
bad.summary: GEMM-Lagos led rescue of an adult female Kogia breviceps at Praia do Forte (22 Jul) after three beachings; Instituto Albatroz CRD care failed on 24 Jul (~3 m, ~350 kg; cookiecutter bites, hypoglycemia). Necropsy ongoing via REMASE/PMP-BC-ES. Rare deep-water species ashore is a research signal and a reminder to call 0800 991 4800 for Lagos strandings.

bad.title: Illegal double trawl seized ~800 m off Camiranga, Ilha Grande Bay
bad.summary: CPAm officers caught a vessel trawling in a restricted zone near Praia da Camiranga (Angra). Live fish were released; crustaceans and the boat were seized and crew taken to the Federal Police. Charged under Lei 9.605/98 art. 34 (fishing in closed areas). Reminder that illegal gear still operates inside the bay’s conservation mosaic.

bad.title: Paranaguá shale-oil leak into storm drains investigated by IAT
bad.summary: IAT and firefighters probed a Cattalini Terminais Marítimos shale-oil release into rain galleries in Serraria da Rocha after odor complaints (mid-Jul). Company said small volume was recovered and did not reach the sea; IAT assessed contamination risk at the port complex feeding Paraná’s coastal estuary — relevant SE shipping/oil exposure adjacent to our brief waters.

bad.title: Oil residues found on Ipanema and at Arraial do Cabo RESEX
bad.summary: Ibama Ceneac collected samples at Ipanema for UFRJ Ladetec analysis; ICMBio reported similar material at Praia Grande (Arraial RESEX). No bathing ban was in place at reporting; avoid touching tar pellets. The Navy Capitanía found no open-water slick at Ipanema. Public origin results were not yet clear through mid-September searches.
